holidays.name: Donald Duck Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the world's most famously short-tempered duck. Celebrate with classic cartoons, your best sputtering Donald impression, and a sailor suit if you're feeling bold.
holidays.origin: Donald Duck made his screen debut on June 9, 1934, in the Disney short "The Wise Little Hen." Fans have marked the anniversary ever since.
holidays.funFact: Donald's first appearance was a supporting role. He went on to star in more films than any other Disney character, and he has long been one of Disney's most popular characters.

holidays.name: National Strawberry Rhubarb Pie Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the sweet-tart pie that pairs juicy strawberries with tangy rhubarb. Bake one from scratch, or buy a slice and tell no one.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It falls in early summer, when rhubarb and strawberries are both in season.
holidays.funFact: Rhubarb is technically a vegetable. Its leaves are toxic, so only the stalks go into the pie.

holidays.name: National Earl Day
holidays.description: A day to salute everyone named Earl, from the Earls in your family tree to the Earl who always has a good story at the barbecue. Give the Earl you know a shout-out, and don't forget Earl Grey tea.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a name-based celebration in the style of other "National [Name] Days."
holidays.funFact: Earl is a rank of British nobility, and it's the one rank that has no feminine form. The wife of an earl is called a countess.
